summary: A class implements Comparable to define one natural order. A Comparator defines any other order, and comparing(...).thenComparing(...) sorts by several fields.
notes: compareTo returns a negative number, zero, or a positive number. name.compareTo(other.name) does that for Strings.
list.sort(null) means use the natural order from compareTo.
pitfall: Writing return other.grade - grade works until values are large enough to overflow int, then the order breaks with no error. Use Integer.compare(other.grade, grade) or comparingInt.
